landmarks.name: Vaduz Castle
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the Prince of Liechtenstein, perched on a hill overlooking the capital Vaduz.

landmarks.name: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein
landmarks.writeup: A modern art museum in Vaduz featuring contemporary and modern art collections.

landmarks.name: Gutenberg Castle
landmarks.writeup: A well-preserved medieval castle located in the town of Balzers.

cultural_events.name: Vaduz Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing international and local films, promoting cultural exchange.

cultural_events.name: National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on August 15th with speeches, fireworks, and traditional festivities.

food_writeup: Liechtenstein cuisine is influenced by Swiss and Austrian traditions, featuring dishes like Käsknöpfle (cheese noodles), Ribel (cornmeal dish), and various hearty meat and potato meals.
brief_history: Liechtenstein was established as a principality in 1719 within the Holy Roman Empire. It remained neutral during both World Wars and developed into a prosperous financial center in the 20th century.

important_people.name: Franz Joseph II
important_people.description: Former Prince who modernized the country
